builtBy: research in two rounds, written by hand from what survived. 2026-10-03, field hockey: four source-family sweeps (commitment lists, NorCal clubs and media, school and local news for each league) and a player-by-player sweep of every junior, senior and ungraded varsity row on the 37 teams with roster rows; every candidate re-opened by a checker and, independently, by a refuter trying to break it; a completeness critic's follow-ups; a final audit that re-opened every source. 2026-10-04, every sport and more field hockey recall: sweeps of SportsRecruits' college pages for field hockey (290), women's lacrosse (643) and women's soccer (1,670) with their committed profiles, a SportsRecruits profile-address probe for all 716 varsity players, FH College Path's six class lists, Stick Together's whole archive, MAX Field Hockey, club commitment lists, lacrosse and soccer commitment databases, other-sport databases, every 2025-26 story of 18 student papers and 8 local papers, and the club-tied players one by one; every candidate again re-opened by a checker and an independent refuter, and the final file's sources re-opened once more. 2026-10-04, the six Eastern Athletic League teams' schools: a field hockey sweep, then the every-sport round over their 95 varsity rows with the same rule and source families (SportsRecruits' college pages for field hockey, women's lacrosse and women's soccer, FH College Path, Stick Together, MAX Field Hockey and the other field hockey lists, TopDrawerSoccer, SoccerWire, ClubLax and the NorCal lacrosse, soccer, volleyball, softball and basketball club lists, MileSplit, the local and student papers that cover these schools, the schools' sites, and two web searches for each junior and senior), with the same day's recruiting-profiles research supplying a SportsRecruits profile-address probe for all 95 in every sport and NCSA and FieldLevel probes for field hockey; it found no commitment, and SportsRecruits' athlete search was not run for those rows
notes: Which players on the tracked varsity rosters (the 43 teams of the four leagues swept on 2026-10-03 and 2026-10-04, and the six Eastern Athletic League teams swept on 2026-10-04) a public page says have committed to play a sport in college, joined to data/rosters.json on team slug + MaxPreps athleteId. Field hockey is the site's sport, but a commitment in any sport counts (since 2026-10-04): many players here also play lacrosse, soccer or basketball, and commit there. Only players on those rosters are named (varsity rows; rows the overlay marks JV, graduates, and players at schools with no MaxPreps rows are out of scope: six of the 43, and Corning, one of the six EAL teams' schools), each under the roster's own spelling.

The linking rule is the one data/clubs.json uses: a public page must name the player and the college in the context of one sport, and either name the player's high school, or give a class year that agrees with the roster grade together with a Northern California location (the player's hometown, or a club or team based in Northern California). A name alone never makes a match, and a class year that disagrees with the roster grade rules one out; two same-name players in one region (two class-of-2027 Phoebe Millers, in Larkspur and San Francisco) are told apart by a page that names the school. College interests, offers, visits, camps, watchlists, a plan to play somewhere ('planning to continue her career at …'), and a place on a college's club team are not commitments.

Social media is never a source (lib/clubs-schema.ts BANNED_HOSTS). Many commitments are announced only there, so a commitment with no other public page is not in this file. Every source names the player or is the player's own recruiting profile; quotes and bases are kept for maintainers and never rendered. A page that draws its list only once a script runs (SportsRecruits' /committed/<club> pages, MAX Field Hockey's search) is not cited, so every quote can be checked against the page's own HTML; STEPS California's page answers plain requests with a bot challenge but serves its table as HTML, which WebFetch reads.

status: 'signed' only where a source says signed; otherwise 'committed'. No source found by 2026-10-04 said any player had signed. asOf: the earliest date a kept source gives for the commitment (a dated story's own date, or the month a story says the player committed), or null. Every kept source was confirmed by two independent reads. A date that only one read saw is not used: MAX Field Hockey's hidden table dates, and the 'Committed to … on M/D/YYYY' tooltip SportsRecruits draws on a profile with a script.

confidence: high = one first-hand page names the player, the college and the school, or it is the player's own recruiting profile showing the commitment; medium = the match rests on one line of a compiled list plus class year and a Northern California club.

The schools of the six Eastern Athletic League teams (Bella Vista, Chico, Corning, Davis, Lassen, Pleasant Valley) were swept twice on 2026-10-04. The first sweep looked for field hockey commitments only (the NFHCA 2026 high school watchlist, the NCFHA youth directory, SportsRecruits profile slugs, fhcollegepath.com classes 2026-2028 and MAX Field Hockey) and found none; the day's every-sport round (see builtBy) had then covered only the 43 teams tracked before. The every-sport round was then extended to their 95 varsity rows (Bella Vista 19, Chico 20, Davis 19, Lassen 15, Pleasant Valley 22; Corning has no roster rows) under the same rule: SportsRecruits' college pages for field hockey (290), women's lacrosse (643) and women's soccer (1,652); FH College Path's class lists; Stick Together's whole archive; HTC's alumnae list; Play College Field Hockey's sheet; the NFHCA watchlist; MAX Field Hockey's table (986 rows, not cited); TopDrawerSoccer's and SoccerWire's California girls' lists for 2027 to 2030; ClubLax's commitments database; NorCal lacrosse, soccer, volleyball, softball and basketball club lists; MileSplit's California signings; a search of each of the 95 names, since January 2025, on the sites of the Chico Enterprise-Record, Red Bluff Daily News, Davis Enterprise, Daily Democrat and Paradise Post (the first 20 results on each of the four WordPress papers), full crawls since January 2025 of the Enterprise-Record's high school section (340 posts) and Red Bluff's high school and local sports sections, and Davis High's and Pleasant Valley's student papers; the schools' sites; and two web searches for each of the 78 juniors and seniors. The same day's recruiting-profiles research ran SportsRecruits' profile-address probe for all 95 rows (1,242 addresses in every sport, 88 live profiles, nine showing a commitment, each another player by class year or state) and NCSA and FieldLevel probes, for field hockey only. It found no commitment in any sport, so the EAL still adds no row. Not run for these rows: SportsRecruits' athlete search, which turned up every commitment in the file that rests on a SportsRecruits profile; the 17 freshmen and sophomores got no web searches; Lassen County's local news sites refused requests. EAL recall is therefore lower than the other leagues', and the absence of a commitment is not proof that none exists.

EAL near misses, none a commitment: three Davis players on the NFHCA 2026 high school watchlist, which names no college; a Davis junior's own field hockey profile, which states a goal to play in college, and a Davis senior's SportsRecruits bio, which says she would love to continue to play at the collegiate level (both plans); a SportsRecruits soccer entry with a Davis senior's exact name whose class year is 2025, which disagrees with the roster grade (another player, in Virginia); the class-of-2026 commitments from Chico, Pleasant Valley and Davis in Stick Together and the Davis Enterprise's May 23, 2026 signing story, whose players have graduated and are not on these rosters; and same-surname entries with another first name, state or class year on SportsRecruits, FH College Path, TopDrawerSoccer and SoccerWire. An Action News Now story on Chico High soccer players committing to Division I (October 28, 2021) names Priscilla Ward and Taylor Dever, neither on these rosters. The Chico and Pleasant Valley 'Athlete Committed' pages are a health program, not college commitments.

Recall is partial: a commitment announced only on social media, on a page the sweeps could not read, or not yet published anywhere is not here. Re-running this is research, not a script; the class of 2027's signing period (November 2026) and the class of 2028's commitments are when it would change most.
